### 📓 Docs Drift Check
This PR changes **3** package(s): `@objectstack/objectql`, `@objectstack/plugin-approvals`, `@objectstack/plugin-audit`, touching **31** documentable anchor(s).

**16** hand-written doc(s) name something this change touched — list omitted above 15 rows. Re-derive on the tree named below: `node scripts/docs-audit/affected-docs.mjs --json 9abc732132a2f723627d585b049e2cc10869db19`.

⛔ **5** release-owned page(s) also affected — read-only, see AGENTS.md Documentation Guardrails.

<details><summary>What this run could not see</summary>

- **2** name(s) were too generic to anchor anything (single lowercase words)
- the SDK route bridge reached **68** of **251** client-bound route-ledger rows — the other **183** have no registrar `path:` tail to select them, so pages documenting THEIR client methods cannot appear above, on this or any run. Of those **183**: **0** are remediable by widening that discovery convention (an in-repo file declares the path; the convention did not scan it); **59** are structural — on a ledger where NOT ONE row is declared in-repo, so no discovery change reaches them at any price; **124** are undecided (no in-repo declaration, on a ledger that has other in-repo registrars — absence and an unreadable spelling are not distinguishable here). The rows themselves: `node scripts/docs-audit/affected-docs.mjs --bridge-coverage`
- a page that states a rule by its **inputs** shares no identifier with the **emitter** that implements the rule, so an emitter-only diff cannot list it — not on this run and not on any run. Measured on #11430: `content/docs/protocol/objectql/types.mdx` documents the text-family column mapping by the ObjectQL type names it maps FROM (`text` / `textarea` / `html`) while the diff changed `createColumn`; it went unlisted, and it was the page that diff falsified, in four places. No shared token exists to detect this on, so a rule your change carries has to be re-read by hand in the pages that restate it.
- a key NAME is not a key, so the hand re-read the line above prescribes can land on the wrong schema. The same spelling is authorable on one governed type and a `[REMOVED]` tombstone on another for each of `active`, `aria`, `joins`, `objects`, `template`, `tools` and `version` (censused on #19093 over the liveness ledger's governed types, top-level keys); nothing in a search result distinguishes the two, so a grep hit on a LIVE example reads as evidence about the DEAD key. Measured on #19059: `content/docs/ai/agents.mdx` was reported as contradicting the `agent.tools` tombstone over its `tools:` example at `:161`, which is inside the `defineSkill({` block opened at `:155` — the page was already correct. Settle ownership by PARSING the value against both schemas, never by the name: that literal PASSES `SkillSchema`, and as an `AgentSchema` it FAILS at `tools` with the tombstone prescription. ⛔ These names are not the whole class — a key retired through a `.strict()` guidance map leaves no tombstone in the walked shape and none of them here (`tool.category`, live as `AIToolDefinition.category`).

Coarse fallback — **32** page(s) merely *mention* a changed package (the pre-#9192 predicate, kept for the deliberately-wide backstop): `node scripts/docs-audit/affected-docs.mjs --json 9abc732132a2f723627d585b049e2cc10869db19` → `packageMentionDocs`.
</details>

<details><summary>Which tree this was computed on</summary>

This run read `content/docs` from `f068f4423f2425fac2e6082aae1acb427f4bd063` — the merge of head `44c8fc39f4c0a3bbed44d384b86345590bb6fd11` into base `9abc732132a2f723627d585b049e2cc10869db19`, which is what `actions/checkout` gives a `pull_request` run. **Not** the PR head.

A worktree cut from an older `main` holds a different `content/docs`, so re-deriving there can legitimately return a different list — that is a **different tree, not a wrong row**. To answer on the same tree:

```sh
# while this PR is open — GitHub drops the merge commit once it closes
git fetch origin f068f4423f2425fac2e6082aae1acb427f4bd063 && git checkout f068f4423f2425fac2e6082aae1acb427f4bd063
# afterwards, rebuild it from the two parents, which stay fetchable
git fetch origin 9abc732132a2f723627d585b049e2cc10869db19 44c8fc39f4c0a3bbed44d384b86345590bb6fd11 && git checkout -B drift-repro 9abc732132a2f723627d585b049e2cc10869db19 && git merge --no-ff 44c8fc39f4c0a3bbed44d384b86345590bb6fd11

node scripts/docs-audit/affected-docs.mjs --json 9abc732132a2f723627d585b049e2cc10869db19
```

⚠️ That checkout carried **uncommitted changes**, so the commit above does not fully identify what was read.
</details>

> Advisory only, and a **precision-first** one (#9192): a page is listed because it names a
> symbol, wire route or SDK method this diff touched — not because it mentions a changed
> package. Each row says which anchor put it there, so a wrong row is reportable rather than
> merely annoying. To re-verify, run the `docs-accuracy-audit` workflow scoped to these files:
> `node scripts/docs-audit/affected-docs.mjs 9abc732132a2f723627d585b049e2cc10869db19` → pass the list as
> `args.docs`, on the commit named under **Which tree this was computed on**.

## 席位核对

L1 (L1-e) on head `67d23afa2c0c9d8093db67494616964f9210498e`, card #35384 (first stage): **ACCEPT**, with one landing condition (body only). No contract face is touched, so no L2 is owed by the face. The seat's own L2 call stands as made.

**Landing condition.** Both new readers hand `translateObject` the metadata route's resolve options but not its packaged base.
- plugin-approvals `objectLabel` passes `{ name }` alone. plugin-audit `translatedObjectDef` passes the served definition without `packagedBase`.
- The meta door passes `packagedObjectBaseOf(p, 'object', name)`, so for a renamed object (a served label that diverged from the packaged one) it serves the rename. These two readers serve the catalog's translation of the old label instead.
- This is not a regression: `t('objects.<o>.label')` did the same before.
- Two new docblocks overclaim it: "resolved as `/meta` resolves it" in `reader-locale-labels.ts` and "put in its language … as `/meta`" in `activity-summary-message.ts`. The changeset is scoped correctly ("with the resolve options the metadata route builds").
- Before landing, file a card for "approval object label and activity-summary labels ignore the packaged base: a renamed object reads the translation of its old label", or fold it into the #35384 remainder already routed in the body. Name it there. Qualifying the two docblocks is a nit, with no new head owed for it.
- For reference, #36460 threaded the base through `getPackagedObjectBase` for the share-link label. The same read would close this.

**Read**
- **Shape** (`l1-face.mjs --pr 36464`): open, draft, base `main`, `Part of #35384`, `Clause-②: no`, `Metadata-protocol: none`, mergeable `clean`. Gates at this head: 39 success, 18 expected skip, 0 failed.
  - The face flags `changeset` for `@objectstack/service-automation`. That touch is one `*.integration.test.ts`, and the build entry is `src/index.ts` (root `tsup.config.ts`) with `files: ['dist', …]`, so nothing ships and no entry is owed.
- **`Part of` is right.** This stage moves three of the card's readers. The approval notification subject param stays open: it is resolved per recipient at delivery through `t()`, and the producer holds no locale. The Acceptance notes route it, with the flow, step and position labels, as the remainder. #36466 (meta door locale negotiation) and #36467 (one exported options builder) are filed.
- **objectql rule message.** `authoredRuleMessage` first keeps an authored message that diverged from the packaged rule (`scalarOverridesPackagedBase`), unchanged. Otherwise it resolves `{ name, validations: [{ name, message }] }` through `translatedLabels` over `labelTranslation`, the same bundle and options the refusal's field and object labels use (#34030), with no second copy. The `t()` key path is gone. The translator throwing still leaves a 400, not a 500.
- **Approvals and audit.** The options match `metaTranslateOptions`: the negotiated locale, the declared fallback, and `sourceLocale` else `defaultLocale`. Each getter is feature-detected, and the build runs once per read and is memoised per object.
  - Audit: the labels are read off the translated definition (`objectLabelIn`, `fieldLabelForSummary`, `optionLabelOn`). `t()` keeps only `messages.*`.
  - The writer's stored sentence is unchanged: `storedSummaryLocale` reads authored definitions with `translate: () => undefined`, as before.
  - A throwing service leaves the authored labels.
- **Changeset, checked sentence by sentence.** It is true, including the stated narrowing: "an i18n service that cannot hand its translations over … no longer has these labels and rule messages translated through `t()`". Every shipped service implements both getters.
